raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# Description

Cutedsl kernels rely on cuda.core to check compute capability, but this is not a TE dependency.

This will make CI able to run using CuTeDSL kernels instead of falling back to CUDA kernels. It also fixes how a all NaN 32 element block is handed so now the scale will be NaN instead of 0 when all elements are NaN, and it's consistent across different configurations for both CUDA and CuTeDSL so the CI tests can pass.

Fixes #3793

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

## Changes

Please list the changes introduced in this PR:

- Replace cuda.core with cuda.bindings
- Fix NaN handling in MXFP8 quantization kernels

# Checklist:

- [ ] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [ ] The functionality is complete
- [ ] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [ ] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

nodes.body: **Backends disagree on NaN scales** Full all-NaN blocks now get scale `0xFF` in the generic CUDA kernel, but CuTeDSL still turns their amax into zero. An all-NaN FP32 input therefore gets different scale bytes from the same quantizer depending on the selected backend. This breaks the bit-exact scale contract checked by the backend comparison tests. Keep the NaN behavior consistent across both backends and add an all-NaN comparison case.

files.patch:
@@ -208,7 +208,9 @@ def quantize_rowwise_mxfp8(
     # and keep the elements in half precision instead of upcasting every one of them to f32.
     USE_HALF_PRECISION = is_packed16(DTYPE) and (ACTIVATION is None or FUSE_RELU)
 
-    amax_r = Float32(0.0)
+    # Initial amax as NaN, which loses all comparisons unless the other value is also NaN,
+    # so per-block amax will be NaN if all values in the block are NaN.
+    amax_r = Float32(float("nan"))
 
     # Each thread start reading from the specfic bank based on its thread ID so they can do their best to access different banks
     # to avoid bank conflict.
@@ -516,12 +518,18 @@ def quantize_colwise_mxfp8(
         if cutlass.const_expr(CACHE_ACTIVATION):
             for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(MXFP8_BLOCK_SCALING_SIZE):
                 sX_thread[i] = DTYPE(rX_thread_f32[i])
-        amax_c = Float32(0.0)
+        # Initial amax as NaN, which loses all comparisons unless the other value is also NaN,
+        # so per-block amax will be NaN if all values in the block are NaN.
+        amax_c = Float32(float("nan"))
         for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(MXFP8_BLOCK_SCALING_SIZE):
             if cutlass.const_expr(FUSE_RELU):
                 amax_c = cute.arch.fmax(amax_c, rX_thread_f32[i])
             else:
                 amax_c = cute.arch.fmax(amax_c, fabs_f32(rX_thread_f32[i]))
+        if cutlass.const_expr(FUSE_RELU):
+            # For relu the max is at least 0
+            # We see relu(nan) = 0.0 here which is consistent with CUDA's relu implementation with fmaxf
+            amax_c = cute.arch.fmax(amax_c, Float32(0.0))
 
     # Irregular shapes: skip when this stage's row range or this thread's
     # column lies past the input extents. TILE_Y == MXFP8_BLOCK_SCALING_SIZE so each stage
@@ -747,7 +755,9 @@ def quantize_bidimensional_mxfp8_swizzled(
         rX = cute.make_rmem_tensor(MXFP8_BLOCK_SCALING_SIZE, Float32)
         cute.autovec_copy(tXsX, rX)
 
-        row_amax = Float32(0.0)
+        # Initial amax as NaN, which loses all comparisons unless the other value is also NaN,
+        # so per-block amax will be NaN if all values in the block are NaN.
+        row_amax = Float32(float("nan"))
         for c in cutlass.range_constexpr(MXFP8_BLOCK_SCALING_SIZE):
             a = fabs_f32(rX[c])
             row_amax = cute.arch.fmax(row_amax, a)

@@ -29,12 +29,26 @@
 
 def device_compute_capability(device_id: Optional[int] = None) -> tuple:
     """(major, minor) compute capability of a CUDA device (current by default), or (0, 0) if it can't be queried."""
-    from cuda.core import Device  # pylint: disable=no-name-in-module
+    # pylint: disable=c-extension-no-member
+    from cuda.bindings import runtime as cudart  # pylint: disable=no-name-in-module
+
+    def check(result):
+        err, *values = result
+        if err != cudart.cudaError_t.cudaSuccess:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"CUDA runtime error {err}")
+        return values[0]
 
     try:
-        device_id = Device().device_id if device_id is None else device_id
-        major_minor = Device(device_id).arch
-        return (int(major_minor[:-1]), int(major_minor[-1])) if major_minor else (0, 0)
+        if device_id is None:
+            device_id = check(cudart.cudaGetDevice())
+        attr = cudart.cudaDeviceAttr
+        major = check(
+            cudart.cudaDeviceGetAttribute(attr.cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor, device_id)
+        )
+        minor = check(
+            cudart.cudaDeviceGetAttribute(attr.cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMinor, device_id)
+        )
+        return (major, minor)
     except Exception as e:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
         logger.warning("Could not query CUDA device compute capability (%s); assuming (0, 0).", e)
         return (0, 0)
